02 Live Data & Exploratory Analysis

Every one of 11,143 events in the window, colour-coded by magnitude — the Ring of Fire dominates. Source: public USGS global feed (no API key).
b = 1.15 ≈ 1.0 — the live data obeys the Gutenberg–Richter law, the fundamental frequency–magnitude rule of seismology. A healthy catalog.
Small events dominate: only 189 of 11,143 (1.7%) are significant (M ≥ 5.0) — yet those drive the response.
Daily activity with 7-day moving average — steady ~370 events/day; no time-of-day effect (earthquakes are 24/7/365).
Deep quakes (>300 km) average M 4.5 vs M 1.6 shallow — a detection bias: only large deep events reach our sensors.

3 of 8 highest-confidence alerts verified significant (37.5% vs 1.5% base rate — 26× better than random). Misses cluster just below M 5.0, where magnitude estimates are least stable. We show the misses on purpose.

04 The Response Platform

DETECT (USGS real-time feed) → SCORE (ML triage, < 1 s) → ZONE (risk lookup) → ALERT (SMS / app to response teams) → DISPATCH (pre-positioned resources).
Only top-confidence, in-risk-zone events page on-call responders — cutting alert noise while catching 79% of significant events.

Honest science: this system does not predict individual earthquakes. It answers two different questions — where should we be ready? (risk zones) and which detected events deserve immediate attention? (ML triage).

05 Key Insights

Gutenberg–Richter b = 1.15 — live data follows the fundamental seismology law (b ≈ 1), validating our catalog
Location + depth = 90% of model signal — the algorithm learned the Ring of Fire on its own, from data alone
Deep quakes (>300 km) average M 4.5 vs M 1.6 shallow — only large deep events are detectable
13.3× lift — flagged events are ~13× more likely to be significant; 79% of future significant events caught
